title: K1698: FTD E1 v2 — scale re-calibration gating (compliant rerun of K1684)
question: Is the K850/K854 QLIKE-vs-VaR divergence an artifact of the variance-target mismatch, once every K1684 review blocker is fixed?
proposer: Codex review of K1684 (BLOCKED 2026-07-12) + Fable deep review §5.1 E1
rv_source: TAIFEX all-contract TX tick -> active-contract, gap-complete, 13:30-aligned 5-min RV
GATE_REASON: leg 1 fails at the Harvey calibre: on the ALIGNED target (0050 r^2) HAR-RV shows no Harvey-significant QLIKE win over the robust GJR (t=1.4694). Without a forecast-loss win on a common target there is no divergence to explain, whatever the tail layer does.
GATE_ROUTE: FRL / Journal of Forecasting SHORT NOTE (divergence is a construction artifact; the diagnostic is the contribution)

preregistered_rules.leg1_forecast_loss: HAR-RV (uncorrected) vs robust GJR, QLIKE scored on the ALIGNED target (0050 r^2), canonical volpred dm_test (h=1, HAC bandwidth ceil(h^(1/3) n^(1/3))). HAR wins iff t < -3 (Harvey). |t| <= 3 means no significant forecast-loss win and leg 1 FAILS. p<0.05 with |t|<=3 is reported but does NOT satisfy leg 1.
preregistered_rules.leg2_baseline_pattern: The K850/K854 divergence pattern must be present under robust estimation: HAR+CF trinity FAIL at 1% AND GJR+CF trinity PASS at 1% (OOS). Explicitly checked in code (K1684 said this but never checked it).
preregistered_rules.rescue: A corrected variant (HAR-a/b/c) rescues HAR iff ANY of its three tail layers passes the FULL trinity at BOTH alpha levels. Kupiec-only coverage at both alphas is reported separately as a secondary (weaker) criterion.
preregistered_rules.verdict: H2_SURVIVES iff leg1 Harvey-win AND leg2 pattern AND 0/estimable variants rescue. H2_REJECTED iff (not leg1) OR (not leg2 pattern) OR (all estimable variants rescue). H2_PARTIAL otherwise.

route.H2_REJECTED: FRL / Journal of Forecasting SHORT NOTE (divergence is a construction artifact; the diagnostic is the contribution)
route.H2_SURVIVES: Full IJF paper (residual orthogonality is real)
route.H2_PARTIAL: Conditional — the H1 decomposition carries the paper either way

preregistered_rules.channel_classification: Distribution-free c_emp(alpha) = (1-alpha) empirical quantile of u = r/VaR, paired moving-block bootstrap (B=2000, block=25, shared index draws across cells and alphas). Classification per cell: SHAPE if 95% CI of delta_c = c(1%)-c(5%) excludes 0; else CALIBRATED if both c CIs contain 1; else SCALE if at least one c CI excludes 1; else AMBIGUOUS.

rv_construction.method: per-day max-volume active TX contract; ONE continuous 5-min path over (13:30(D-1), 13:30(D)] incl. day-tail, 13:45->15:00 gap, PM->AM night, 05:00->08:45 gap; no cross-contract returns

boundary_audit.implication: RV(D) window is (13:30(D-1), 13:30(D)] with the anchor price AT 13:30(D-1): as a predictor, RV(t-1) ends exactly where the 0050 close-to-close target window for day t begins — the information sets are disjoint by construction (13:30/13:45 overlap sealed).

old_vs_new.note: old = K854 TX1 trade-date-convention RV (separate session sums, no boundary jumps); new = aligned active-contract gap-complete RV

lookahead_audit.method: x10 perturbation of every observation at index >= origin; origin forecasts and correction parameters must return bit-identical

fragility_probe_v2.perturbation: returns x (1 + N(0, 1e-6)), 6 seeded draws, refit start seeds held fixed (isolates the data effect)

k854_replication_bridge.note: Bridge run = old TX1 RV + ROBUST (120-start) GJR/RGL on the common evaluation sample. Differences on GJR/RGL cells quantify what the 4-start MLE instability was worth; HAR-cell differences (if any) come from the common-sample intersection with the new RV calendar.

basel_caliber.1pct: STANDARD Basel 250-day count rule (green <=4, yellow 5-9, red >=10) on the last 250 days of the OOS window.
basel_caliber.5pct: CUSTOM alpha-scaled extension (green <=20, yellow <=45) — NOT canonical Basel (defined at 1% only). Inherited from K854 and flagged as custom.

limitations: n = 450 < the >=500 house rule at the OOS stage; ~4.5 expected violations at 1% mean low Kupiec power and single-violation Basel flips. Exact CP bands and bootstrap CIs are reported everywhere. The IS window (n~1000, includes COVID) partially compensates but is in-sample by construction.
One market (0050.TW), one calm OOS regime (2023-2024). External validity of the scale channel needs E2 (SPY) / E5 (third market).
The three theta estimators share the same r^2/RV data — reported as three estimators of one wedge, not independent evidence.
The 5% Basel light is a custom extension, not a regulatory standard.
CF expected shortfall integrates the (possibly non-monotone) Cornish-Fisher quantile polynomial; FZ0 rows with es >= var are dropped and counted.
Returns are simple pct_change on adjusted closes; RV uses log returns (second-order difference at daily frequency).
Skewed-t anchor tail fit keeps K854's single-start estimator (2 params, bounded), unlike the >=100-start GJR/RGL variance MLEs.
references: McNeil & Frey (2000, J Empirical Finance 7) — ES exceedance residual test
Acerbi & Szekely (2014, Risk) — direct ES backtests (Z2)
Fissler & Ziegel (2016, Ann. Statist. 44) — joint VaR-ES elicitability (FZ0)
Gonzalez-Rivera, Lee & Mishra (2004, IJF 20); Bams et al. (2017, IJF 33)
